segments.he: צָרִיךְ לְהַכְנִיס הַחֲמִימוּת הַבּוֹעֵר בַּלֵּב לִתְפִלּוֹת וּצְעָקוֹת
segments.en: As is written in the Midrash Rabbah on Parashas Korach: Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira says: the assembly of Korach is destined to ascend. It is written about them: "and they perished from the midst of the congregation" [Bamidbar 16:33] — and Dovid says: "I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant" [Tehillim 119:176]. Just as the lost thing spoken of with Dovid is destined to be sought, so too here the lost thing is destined to be sought. That is: the primary rectification of Korach and his assembly is through this very thing — through the aspect of King Dovid who composed the Book of Tehillim, and through all those who cleave to him and walk in his ways and engage in the Book of Tehillim and supplications and many petitions and many conversations and hisbodidus between themselves and their Maker — and cry out each time: "I have strayed like a lost sheep, seek Your servant." For anyone who has compassion on his soul will understand within himself how very much he must cry out: "I have strayed like a lost sheep, seek Your servant" — if King Dovid, who was such a Tzaddik, cried out "I have strayed like a lost sheep" — then with how many thousands and tens of thousands of times stronger an argument must we cry out such cries, perhaps we will be able to find ourselves. And one who walks in this path rectifies the flaw of Korach — for they disputed against these good longings described above, which is the aspect of the path of prayer and hisbodidus that is the very completion of the true Tzaddik. Therefore through the aspect of "I have strayed like a lost sheep" — through the aspect of Dovid and those who cleave to him, who engage in this: to beseech Hashem to seek them and restore their loss — they certainly will be sought in the end. And even the assembly of Korach who opposed the upright ones — for wherever there is dispute, there are the sparks of Korach, Dasan, and Aviram, as is brought in the holy books — even so, ultimately they are destined to be sought through the service of the upright ones who engage in Tehillim and hisbodidus and cry out each time "I have strayed like a lost sheep" — for through this they will certainly in the end be sought, and even all who dispute and are distant will ascend. For they will return to us, and we shall not return to them — for the truth of Hashem is forever.

segments.he: וְעִקַּר הַנֵּס שֶׁל פּוּרִים הָיָה עַל יְדֵי מָרְדְּכַי עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַצְּעָקוֹת וּזְעָקוֹת שֶׁצָּעַק לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהִכְנִיס גַּם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְעק וְלִצְעק הַרְבֵּה לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ כִּי אֵין שׁוּם עֵצָה נֶגְדָּם כִּי אִם עַל יְדֵי זֶה. כִּי אֵין כּחֵנוּ אֶלָּא בַּפֶּה. כִּי הֵם מִתְגָּרִים בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בְּכַמָּה וְכַמָּה בְּחִינוֹת עַד שֶׁרוֹצִים לְהַכְנִיס חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כַּעַס וְחֵמָה בֵּין יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעַצְמָן וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה רוֹצִים לִטְרף הַשֶּׁפַע מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל חַס וְשָׁלוֹם וּלְהִתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם כַּנַּ"ל. וְעַל כֵּן אֵין עֵצָה וְתַחְבּוּלָה כִּי אִם לִצְעק הַרְבֵּה לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וּלְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְהִתְחַנֵּן אֵלָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ בִּבְחִינַת חַם לִבִּי בְּקִרְבִּי בַּהֲגִיגִי תִּבְעַר אֵשׁ דִּבַּרְתִּי בִלְשׁוֹנִי שֶׁצְּרִיכִין לַהֲפךְ הַחֲמִימוּת הַבּוֹעֵר בַּלֵּב מֵרִבּוּי הַצָּרוֹת שֶׁרוֹצֶה לְהַכְנִיס כַּעַס חַס וְשָׁלוֹם לַהֲפךְ הַכּל לִתְפִלּוֹת וּתְחִנּוֹת וּבַקָּשׁוֹת וּצְעָקוֹת לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּחֲמִימוּת הַלֵּב בִּבְחִינַת חַם לִבִּי וְכוּ'. דִּבַּרְתִּי בִלְשׁוֹנִי כַּנַּ"ל.
segments.en: This is the true path for everyone who wishes to approach the holy and draw close to Hashem — that the primary thing is to multiply prayer and conversation between oneself and one's Maker, as already explained many times. But even this itself is very burdensome. Therefore one must first wait an hour and stand as if mute — only to yearn and look and lift one's eyes above that He flow warm words to one, and to settle one's mind well: where is one in the world, and where has one strayed? Until through this itself one's heart will be warmed and one will speak with the warmth of holiness, in the aspect of: "I was dumb in silence" [Tehillim 39:3] — through this precisely: "my heart was hot within me; as I mused, a fire blazed up; I spoke with my tongue" [ibid. 39:4]. In His mercy he will begin to speak warm words like fire. And this is the aspect of: "for love is as strong as death... its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of G-d" [Shir HaShirim 8:6] — specifically through the very love and longing with which we yearn for Hashem, in the aspect of "love is as strong as death" — through this: "its sparks are sparks of fire" — through this one draws down the sparks of fire described above, in the aspect of warm words like coals of fire.

segments.he: וְזֶהוּ בְּחִינַת מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב שָׁם בִּתְחִלַּת סִימָן נ"ט הַנַּ"ל שֶׁעִקַּר תִּקּוּן הֵיכַל הַקּדֶשׁ הוּא עַל יְדֵי מִשְׁפָּט שֶׁיִּשְׁפּט אֶת עַצְמוֹ עַל כָּל דָּבָר. דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיִּתְבּוֹדֵד וְיַעֲשֶׂה חֶשְׁבּוֹן עִם נַפְשׁוֹ וְיִשְׁפּט אֶת עַצְמוֹ וִיפָרֵשׁ שִׂיחָתוֹ לִפְנֵי ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּחֲמִימוּת הַלֵּב עַד שֶׁיִּתְעוֹרֵר אֵשׁ הַמִּשְׁפָּט וְיִשְׂרף אֶת הָרַע שֶׁל הַנְּפָשׁוֹת שֶׁמְּקָרְבָם וְכוּ' עַיֵּן שָׁם.
segments.en: The general principle is that every person who wishes to have compassion on himself and begin each time to think of his purpose and his end in truth — the primary remedy is through conversation between oneself and one's Maker, in all the paths of counsel described above. And one who is wise in understanding will understand within himself, according to the time and moment, how to have compassion on oneself in truth through the paths described above — for it is impossible to explain all this properly. Only one who truly desires to have compassion on himself and improve his future end will understand many things on his own from these words of ours. For one must not force the hour, as above — yet even so one must hasten greatly to save one's soul. Therefore the primary way is the path described above — the aspect of the Counting of the Omer, where one does not force the hour, but waits seven complete weeks. Yet on each day and each week of the seven weeks one does not let one's mind off seeking and asking and looking and waiting for His very great mercies — to draw upon oneself each day and each hour the aspect of warm words. And through this one draws each day the illumination of the receiving of the Torah — a little each day and each week.

The primary matter of this waiting and tarrying — that one must wait and look greatly and multiply prayer and supplication and conversation greatly until one merits to draw upon oneself the holiness of Torah as described above — involves a great test, and it is almost as if the primary free choice depends on this. For it is well known that everyone desires to fear Your Name — and even the worst of the worst, as long as he is not counted among those who have thrown off the yoke entirely, Heaven forbid, he certainly desires and longs greatly to return to Hashem, even if he has fallen and distanced himself as he has distanced himself. As it is written: "for love is as strong as death... its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of G-d; great waters cannot quench the love, nor can rivers sweep it away" [Shir HaShirim 8:6–7] — as Rashi explains there: this is said of the love of every single person in Yisrael for their Father in Heaven. Only the primary obstacle is that one must wait greatly and multiply prayer and supplication and greatly strengthen oneself in everything that comes upon one. Therefore many were unable to stand in this test and became lax in attending to their eternal lives — until they distanced themselves as they distanced themselves, Heaven forbid. And even all those whom Hashem helps and who remain fixed in their holiness, not letting themselves fall or become lazy, Heaven forbid, from multiplying supplications — pouring out their hearts each day like water in everything that comes upon them — they too would have had no power to strengthen and wait, except through the power of the holy Torah that we have already received collectively at the time of the giving of the Torah, and through the true Torah innovations we receive in every generation from the true Tzaddikim — who in their great and awesome holiness draw down Torah with such great compassion that from their holiness it flows upon us as well, giving us power also to strengthen and wait and wait and multiply supplications and conversation until Hashem looks down from Heaven and sees.
